THE PENAL CODE, 1860

( ACT NO. XLV OF 1860 )

[6th October, 1860]

CHAPTER XVII OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY

Cheating

415. Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, is said to "cheat".

Explanation.- A dishonest concealment of facts is a deception within the meaning of this section.

Illustrations

(a) A, by falsely pretending to be in the Civil Service, intentionally deceives Z. A cheats.

Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property

420. Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

CHAPTER XVI OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY

1[Punishment for hurt by dangerous substance

1[326A. (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt by means of any corrosive substance shall be punished with death, or with imprisonment for life.

(2) The Court may order the fine to be paid to the victim.

Provided that nothing in this section applies to lawful medical treatment.]

Punishment for wrongful restraint

341. Whoever wrongfully restrains any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to 2[five hundred taka], or with both.

Punishment for wrongful confinement

342. Whoever wrongfully confines any person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

  1. 1 Section 326A was inserted by the Penal Code (Second Amendment) Act, 1984 (Act No. XXIV of 1984), with effect from 1st July, 1984
  2. 2 The words "five hundred taka" were substituted for the words "five hundred rupees" by section 3 of the Penal Code (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. X of 1982)
